blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A colleague drops the alternative row of a pump station's group. The new plan both overhauls and replaces the station in 2029, and its NPV is $90k higher. The NPVs in the data value each option on its own. What is the $90k?

options.text: Real value, since each option's NPV is computed on its own and both are now earned
options.says: Both options remove the same risk; with values set for each option alone, the second one's value is risk already removed.

options.text: Real value, but only because the two projects start in the same year
options.says: The year is not the issue: the plan counts two options' values for one asset in any years.

options.text: Value counted twice, since each option's NPV assumes it is done alone
options.says: Right: as with A001's replace and repair in 2028, the $137k there was risk reduction counted twice.

options.text: Rounding by the solver, since each option's binary is solved on its own
options.says: Both variables are exactly 1 in the plan; the objective adds both NPVs in full, so no rounding is involved.

origin.section: Alternatives for One Asset Share One At-Most-One Row

questions.stem: A cable's group has an overhaul O and a replacement P. The model adds a binary k with the row started(O) + started(P) + k = 1 and the objective term -400 k. The plan funds neither O nor P. What are k and its effect on the objective?

options.text: k = 0, and the objective holds no term at all for the cable
options.says: With O and P unfunded, the equality needs k = 1; k = 0 would leave the row at 0 = 1.

options.text: k = 1, and the objective is 400 lower for keeping the cable
options.says: Right: the equality forces k = 1, and -400 k charges the risk of keeping, as risk_G001 did for A001.

options.text: k = 1, and the objective is 400 higher for the money not spent
options.says: The term is -400 k: keeping lowers the objective by the risk carried; saved money shows up only through the budget rows.

options.text: k is 0 or 1, and the objective changes only if k is 1
options.says: The row is an equality, not an inequality, so k is fixed by the other two variables.

origin.section: Doing Nothing Is an Alternative Too, and It Has a Price

questions.stem: A repair may start in 2030, 2031 or 2032; a replacement may follow it if it starts at least 3 years after the repair, and never comes before it. Which repair years conflict with a replacement in 2034?

options.says: Right: a repair in year s conflicts when s > t - G = 2031, so only 2032; 2031 is exactly 3 years earlier and is allowed.
A replacement exactly G years after the repair is allowed, so 2031 is not in the set: the condition is s > t - G.

options.text: None, since every repair year is before 2034
options.says: Being earlier is not enough; a repair in 2032 is only 2 years before 2034.

options.text: All three, since the two options exclude each other
options.says: That is the alternative row, which the gap rows replace because it forbids every sequence.
